cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a Sámi shaman's bowl drum (goavddis) made of a hollowed wood bowl with reindeer skin head, painted with characteristic alder-bark symbols depicting cosmological and spirit-world imagery — a well-documented, distinctive Sámi ritual/musical object.

physical.title: drum
physical.summary:
Drum made of wood and skin, of bowl-drum type, the bowl carved from a single piece of pinewood, with reindeer skin stretched across. The skin is covered in painted designs using ink made from chewed alder bark, and depicting maps, guides and accounts of journeys to the worlds of spirits and gods. Grip at rear formed by two oblong openings cut out of the bowl.
        The skin is strengthened at the edges with thread made of skin, then held with wood pegs round the sides, and sewn on through holes pierced in the bowl. |The thread passes through the sides and the back of the bowl. Metal nails at three points provide further reinforcement.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a Sámi shaman's frame drum (goavddis) with reindeer-skin membrane bearing faint painted/incised ritual figures, a well-documented traditional Sámi instrument used in noaidi ceremonies.

physical.title: drum; religious/ritual equipment
physical.summary:
Drum, made of wood and skin, of frame drum type, with painted designs and figures on membrane for use in magic ceremonies. The reindeer skin membrane bound at the edge and sewn onto the wood frame with a thread made of skin. Some of the motifs on the membrane are inscised as well as coloured, especially those round the outer edge. The frame formed of a single curved piece of wood, which overlaps at one side and is bound with white metal lozenge-shaped rivets, a leather thong, and a brass strip with copper rivets. At top of frame is a rectangular recess, echoed by a rectangular hole of the same size at the bottom of the frame, to take bar of wood as a handle (lacking). The exterior of the frame decorated with incised lines. At the bask, at the wider end hang amulets in the form of leather cords, threaded through the frame; these divide into three cords formed of twisted leather strips and bound with metal wire.  
     A nineteenth century circular label on the frame reads: 'Pres'd by A.W. Franks 1 1869. Klemm Coll.'

cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Sámi (Lapland) shaman drum — pear-shaped wooden frame drum with membrane, here seen from the back showing the carved bone strip and leather thong grip/handle characteristic of these ritual drums; the museum's own early labels confirm "Lapland Magical Drum."

physical.title: drum; religious/ritual equipment
physical.summary:
Magical drum made of carved wood, membrane, bone and leather. A pear-shaped body, pierced with a double hole with a bone strip across the central divide and with leather thongs tied across it. The membrane sewn to the body and painted with various magical motifs. 
       Two early labels: 
a) at the top a handwritten circular BM label recoring the number and donor: '+4344  Lapland  Magical Drum.  H. Willett  3.6.89'
b) below a calligaphic label of laid paper, late 18th or early 19th century:  'Lapland Magical Drum'.
